meta.title: PyroTrace | Satellite data to understand fire activity
meta.description: Explore fire activity across Central America with accessible maps and calendars. PyroTrace connects open MODIS and VIIRS records for learning, research, and planning.

hero.description: Explore where and when burning activity concentrates across Central America. Over 25 years of MODIS and VIIRS detections, harmonized for comparison across maps, calendars, and statistics.
hero.assuranceAccessible: Built for everyone, not just GIS experts
hero.coverage: All seven Central American countries, since 2000

continuity.subtitle: VIIRS detects many smaller fires that MODIS misses. Adding raw counts directly makes years since 2012 look artificially higher. Harmonization bridges that gap.
continuity.modisAria: Diagram of an approximate 1 km MODIS pixel grid
continuity.modisDesc: The long historical record: over two decades to track how fire regimes evolve.
continuity.viirsAria: Diagram of a finer 375 m VIIRS pixel grid
continuity.viirsDesc: Higher spatial detail and sensitivity, producing more detections for the same fire.

steps.title: Match
steps.text: We pair MODIS and VIIRS detections of the same fire: within 2.2 km and less than one hour apart.

steps.title: Weight each detection
steps.text: Each VIIRS detection is split across the active VIIRS satellites that year. A MODIS detection also seen by VIIRS gets weight 0 to avoid double-counting. A MODIS-only detection receives a time-of-day factor calibrated per country from post-2012 overlaps.

steps.title: Sum
steps.text: The harmonized index is the sum of these weights in VIIRS-equivalent detections, making a year like 2005 directly comparable to 2024.

continuity.sampleSrCaption: Weight assigned to each detection in the example
continuity.sampleNote: 6.12 is the afternoon reference factor; each country uses its own calibrated factor when enough overlaps exist. Methodology remains under active validation.
continuity.lineText: raw detection counts and the harmonized index.

audience.subtitle: There are many ways to look at a landscape. PyroTrace brings satellite observation closer to everyone who wants to learn, investigate, and plan.

items.title: Curiosity is enough.
items.body: Get started with satellite Earth observation and explore fire activity without advanced GIS training. Clear explanations guide you at every step.

items.title: More room to investigate.
items.body: Students, educators, and researchers: explore the historical record, inspect data sources, and export filtered CSV datasets for classes and studies.

items.title: Territory, with context.
items.body: Environmental analysts, protected-area teams, firefighters, and emergency planners: spot patterns, anomalies, and critical seasons to guide preparedness.

audience.missionBody: Provide free access to and clear understanding of satellite fire-activity data by integrating and harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS records through intuitive maps and calendars that help enthusiasts, students, researchers, and environmental managers identify patterns, anomalies, and critical periods for preventive planning.
audience.visionBody: Become a reference platform that bridges multi-generation satellite records and turns them into clear, comparable, and accessible intelligence—empowering people and organizations to understand fire activity and strengthen research, preparedness, and land management.

team.bodyAfter: challenge at NASA Space Apps 2026: bridging two generations of sensors so fire activity can be compared consistently over time and explored by anyone.

pillars.title: Integration & continuity
pillars.text: We bridge MODIS and VIIRS so sensor differences do not break long-term analysis.

pillars.title: Clarity
pillars.text: We turn complex satellite archives into readable maps and calendars.

pillars.title: Accessibility
pillars.text: A free, approachable experience for everyone from curious learners to institutions.

pillars.title: Rigor & transparency
pillars.text: We validate our methods and clearly document data provenance and ongoing work.

pillars.title: Actionable insight
pillars.text: We help decision-makers recognize patterns, anomalies, and critical fire seasons.

team.partners: We build on open NASA FIRMS data and welcome collaborators across universities, environmental agencies, conservation groups, and technology partners.

questions.subtitle: Clarity starts with explaining how the data works, what it shows, and where its limits are.

items.title: What can I explore in the dashboard?
items.text: Fire detections across all seven Central American countries since November 2000, on an interactive map with filters by date, sensor, and drawn area. The statistics panel compares each month against its historical range and shows annual activity as raw counts or harmonized index.

items.title: What does harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS mean?
items.text: Converting detections from both sensors onto a common scale—VIIRS-equivalent detections—so a year like 2005 can be compared fairly against 2024. The method is outlined above and remains under active validation.

items.title: Why do 2026 records look different?
items.text: Near-real-time detections from 2026 have not yet passed through the historical harmonization pipeline. The explorer marks them separately as provisional and excludes them from multi-year baseline comparisons.

items.title: Is every detection a separate fire?
items.text: No. Each detection is a satellite pixel showing anomalous thermal radiation. One large wildfire can produce many detections, while small or cloud-obscured fires may not be captured.

items.title: Do I need technical expertise?
items.text: Not at all. Start with curiosity: pick a period, inspect the patterns, and read the in-app guides. PyroTrace is built for students and enthusiasts as well as researchers and emergency planners.

items.title: Is the platform free?
items.text: Yes. You can explore without an account and export filtered detections to CSV. We use open NASA FIRMS data and document data provenance and limitations clearly.

items.title: How is PyroTrace sustained?
items.text: Core access remains free. Long-term sustainability relies on community donations, environmental research and innovation grants, technology sponsorships, and partnerships with universities and agencies.

stats.title: Statistics
stats.metricHelpHarmonized: Harmonized index weights MODIS detections so years before and after the 2012 VIIRS launch can be compared on one scale. Experimental index, not a fire count.
stats.metricHelpRaw: Raw MODIS and VIIRS detections. VIIRS adds many small fires from 2012 on, so earlier years read low on this scale.
stats.areaHelp: Showing all regions. To compare a specific place, collapse this panel and draw an area on the map.

stats.guideStep2: Change Reference year or Metric (Detections vs. Harmonized index) to compare periods.
